videos.title: Introducing dots, always-on agents built to handle everything.
videos.description:
Dots are frontier intelligence that have your back. Powered by GPT‑6 Astra, they have their own cloud computer, learn from feedback over time, and can work towards your goals 24/7. Through our ecosystem of plugins, they can readily connect to over 4,000 apps, giving them the tools to help wherever you need them.

Your dot is always within reach, whether it is through ChatGPT, Slack, or Teams. You can ask questions, explore ideas, and give feedback along the way; or you can simply hop on a voice call when you need to talk something out. The more you work together, the more your dot learns your preferences, how you think, and what good looks like to you.

The magic of dots is when they bring you work done the way you would do it, sometimes before you even think to ask. With dots alongside you, ambitious ideas and projects you haven’t had the time or support to pursue start to feel achievable.

https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/

videos.title: Get Stuff Done with ChatGPT Voice
videos.description:
We heard you loud and clear. 

ChatGPT Voice can now:
- Use plugins like your email, calendar, and Slack.

- Be powered by GPT-6 Astra, Sol, and Luna.

- Be used in ChatGPT Work on web and mobile, so you can create docs, decks, sites, and spreadsheets or tackle complex tasks in the browser, just by talking.

Rolling out globally today in the latest version of the app.

videos.title: Figma Gave GPT-6 Astra a Moonshot. Here's what happened.
videos.description:
John gave GPT-6 Astra a moonshot: design the flight-control experience for a new personal aircraft.

The gap between generating an interface and designing a system is massive, and AI models have always fallen short.

Until now.

Astra reasoned through the audience, jobs to be done, pilot-versus-passenger tradeoffs, and critical interface states. Then it connected that thinking to a real design system via the Figma MCP Server to create a polished, on-brand prototype of the concept.

videos.title: One Prompt. A Feature Built and Tested. | Ramp × GPT-6 Astra
videos.description:
Veeral gave GPT-6 Astra a one-line feature request: add routing controls for individual API keys. Astra found the right settings, made the changes, and used computer use to check its own work. It verified the mobile experience without being asked.

About 12 minutes of implementing. 

Another 15 for validating.

Veeral told Romain Huet that was the shift: give Astra a high-level goal, let it make progress, and come back to changes you can review. 

We're making moves. This is why Astra is the next generation in intelligence at work.

videos.title: “A Staff Engineer Collaborator” | Notion’s First Look at GPT-6 Astra
videos.description:
Don’t sleep on Astra. Quinn Johnson started working with GPT-6 Astra differently in Codex: he shared the goal, added context, and let it tackle the problem his team had been working on. On a cache-reuse audit, Astra connected patterns the Notion team had overlooked, then explained the issue clearly. 

The Notion issue was sneaky: older messages were being regenerated using what the agent knew, subtly changing the prompt history and breaking cache reuse. 

Everything could still appear to work while becoming quietly slower and more expensive at scale.  🚀 Astra finding that hidden pattern made it a meaningful engineering win.

videos.title: “A Jaw Drop. Literally.” How Cooley Is Reimagining IPOs with OpenAI
videos.description:
“How do we save time and effort and energy for our clients?”

For David Wang, Cooley’s Chief Innovation Officer, that question is central to IPO preparation, when information requests, drafting sessions, and reviews place heavy demands on senior executives.

With GO Public, built on OpenAI technology, Cooley can get substantive work in front of clients sooner and spot issues earlier. People remain responsible for reviewing the output and standing behind the answers.

videos.title: GPS, explained by Claude Opus 5.5
videos.description: The satellites never hear a word from your phone. Each one broadcasts the time from an atomic clock, over and over, and your phone does the rest: four signals, four distances, and one solve for both where it is and what time it really is. Claude built the interactive page shown here, a true simulation of the real satellites from the published GPS almanac, not a live radio capture.

videos.title: Claude Opus 5.5 rebuilds Earthrise in 3D, down to the second
videos.description:
The Moon's jagged horizon in the 1968 Earthrise photo, and the Earth's place beside it, only look like that from one spot on Apollo 8's path, and that spot gives away the moment. Claude traced 2,781 points along the horizon, matched them against lunar elevation data, and worked out the time and place: 16:39:39 UTC on Dec. 24, 1968, about 69 miles above the Moon. Then it rebuilt the scene in 3D and blinked it against the original.

Photo: NASA, Apollo 8 frame AS08-14-2383 (film scan: NASA/JSC/Arizona State University). Data: NASA LRO LOLA · SLDEM2015 (LOLA + JAXA Kaguya TC) · LROC WAC · NASA GRAIL GL0420A · JPL NAIF · USNO · Apollo 8 Mission Report & Suppl. 1 · NASA SP-201 · NASA TN D-6082 · NASA Earth Observatory Blue Marble · ISCCP (NOAA NCEI) · GEBCO. No endorsement by NASA or any other data provider is implied.

videos.title: Claude Opus 5.5 builds daydreams that hold together
videos.description: Describe a model or drop in a photo, and Claude designs it in bricks where every piece is actually connected, then you get the full step-by-step manual. The app's engine turns the design into parts and checks every connection, because studs grip and side-by-side contact holds nothing. The 2,874-piece Canal Clock Square takes 487 steps across 498 pages, with 15,880 stud joints and not one flagged as weak. Some sections of the demo have been accelerated for time.

videos.title: Claude Opus 5.5 turns graphite into gravity
videos.description: Claude read a hand-drawn catapult part by part, set the scale by taking the drawn blocks as 40 mm wide, and stood the sketch up as a wooden model on the same sheet. After release, every flight and fall is simulated physics, not scripted motion. The first throw falls short, so the sketch gets more lead (the counterweight goes from 0.48 to 0.68 kg), and the second knocks 7 of 10 blocks down, replayed at quarter speed.

videos.title: Claude Cowork and chat are now one Claude
videos.description:
You don't have to choose between chat and Claude Cowork anymore. Ask Claude a quick question or hand it a bigger task, and it brings in whatever the task needs.
Meaghan Choi, who leads design for Claude apps, on why keeping bigger work in a separate place stopped making sense, and what stays put: your chats, tasks, skills and memories are where you left them.
Hand Claude last week's numbers and ask for the deck, and it builds it in the same chat. The work comes back as something you can edit. Claude does the work. You keep the final say.

Read more: https://claude.com/blog/cowork-is-now-claude
